production.format_and_medium.summary: Records maintained in an electronic data processing system or database shall be made available at a reasonable cost not exceeding actual cost; where databases combine exempt and nonexempt records, the body shall provide access to the nonexempt records.

The body shall produce nonexempt database records in any tangible medium identified by the requester — including, where it has the capability, posting on a website or delivery to a requester-provided email address — if that medium is used in the regular course of business.

payment.method.summary: Any local public body that charges for producing records may provide an electronic method of payment (noncash, non-paper-check — credit/debit cards, direct deposit/debit, electronic checks, telephonic payment).

production.no_duty_to_create_or_convert.summary: No public body is required to create a new record that does not already exist, but it may abstract or summarize information under terms agreed with the requester.

No public body is required to produce records from an electronic database in a format not regularly used by it, but it shall make reasonable efforts to provide records in any format under terms agreed with the requester, including payment of reasonable costs.

eligibility.requester_class_restriction.summary: Public records are open only to citizens of the Commonwealth and to representatives of newspapers/magazines with circulation in, and radio/TV stations broadcasting in or into, the Commonwealth; the engine may restrict standing to these requester classes.

intake.identity_requirement.summary: The custodian may require the requester to provide his name and legal address.

eligibility.no_purpose_requirement.summary: A requester need not state a purpose or reason to obtain public records; the custodian may require only the requester's name and legal address.

dup.color.rate.notes: No color-specific rate anywhere in the chapter; the same actual-cost-of-duplication ceiling governs. City may set a distinct color rate provided it does not exceed actual cost.

dup.oversized.rate.label: Copy rate — oversized / nonstandard page
dup.oversized.rate.notes: No oversized/nonstandard-specific rate in the chapter; actual-cost-of-duplication ceiling governs any oversized rate the city sets.

dup.specialty.rate.label: Specialty reproduction (photos, maps, transcripts)
dup.specialty.rate.notes: Specialty reproduction falls under the general actual-cost ceiling. No graduated page-band provision anywhere. A city may adopt volume tiers only insofar as each tier stays within actual cost (VA-…

labor.review.rate.label: Labor rate — review / redaction ($/hr)
labor.review.rate.notes: No separate review/redaction rate or express authorization. If chargeable at all, it is bounded by actual cost incurred and by the surplus-fee prohibition (VA-0023). Flagged for manual verification against FOIA Council opinions.

labor.programming.rate.label: Labor rate — programming / data extraction ($/hr)
labor.programming.rate.notes: Database/electronic extraction is priced at reasonable cost not to exceed actual cost (subsection G, new row VA-9001). labor.billableWhen.unit: enum(never|always|threshold) — no page/hour threshold, no paper-only scope
labor.billableWhen.notes: Labor (accessing/searching/supplying time) is chargeable from the first minute — no free-hours trigger, no page threshold, no paper-only limitation — always subject to the actual-cost ceiling, the lowest-possible-cost duty, and the surplus-fee prohibition. TRAP honored: SB 56 (2026), which would …

labor.overheadPct.label: Overhead / fringe surcharge on labor (%)
labor.overheadPct.notes: An overhead/fringe percentage surcharge cannot exist under Virginia law: charges are capped at actual cost incurred, and surplus fees recouping general costs are expressly prohibited. The configurable % is therefore moot for VA cities.

labor.increment.label: Labor time increment + rounding
labor.increment.notes: Coverage: § 2.2-3704(A)-(J) full text read; § 2.2-3704.1 opened; no administrative fee rule exists. No time-increment or rounding provision. Any increment the city uses must not push charges above actual cost incurred.

rules.freeLaborHours.label: Free labor hours per request
rules.freeLaborHours.notes: Coverage: § 2.2-3704(A)-(J) full text read; § 2.2-3704.1 opened. No free-labor-hours allowance in current law. TRAP: SB 56 (2026) — which proposed free labor hours — passed the Senate but was NOT enacted; its content is deliberately excluded. History line of § 2.2-3704 ends 2023 c. 534.

labor.periodicFreeHours.notes: Coverage: § 2.2-3704(A)-(J) full text read; § 2.2-3704.1 opened. No TX § 552.275-style per-requestor periodic free-time ledger exists in Virginia FOIA.

rules.estimateNotifyThreshold.label: Itemized estimate / cost notice required above ($ or hours)

estimate.requesterResponseDays.label: Requester must respond to an estimate within N days (else withdrawn)
estimate.requesterResponseDays.unit: days from sending of the cost estimate (requester non-response deems the request withdrawn)
estimate.requesterResponseDays.notes: Statute-fixed 30 days (added by 2021 Sp. Sess. I c. 483 era amendments; current through 2023 c. 534). Companion clock rule: the body's response period is tolled between cost-estimate notice and the requester's response (VA-9003). The statute does not specify business vs. calendar days for this 30…

estimate.revisionNotifyPercent.notes: Coverage: § 2.2-3704(A)-(J) full text read; § 2.2-3704.1 opened. No revised-estimate-on-variance requirement. Final charges are independently bounded by actual cost regardless of the estimate.

estimate.validityDays.label: Estimate validity period (days)
estimate.validityDays.notes: Coverage: § 2.2-3704(A)-(J) full text read; § 2.2-3704.1 opened. No estimate-validity period. The 30-day non-response withdrawal (VA-9002) binds the requester's reply window, not how long the estimate's figures remain honored.

rules.deposit.threshold.notes: State-fixed $200 trigger; deposit is permissive ('may'). Deposit is credited toward the final cost (VA-9006) and the response clock tolls while the requester's response to the advance determination is pending (VA-9005).

rules.deposit.percent.label: Deposit capped at (% of estimate)
rules.deposit.percent.unit: % of the advance cost determination (statute states the cap as 'not to exceed the amount of the advance determination', not as a percentage)
rules.deposit.percent.notes: The deposit ceiling equals the full advance determination (i.e., up to 100% of the estimated charges); the city may require any deposit at or under that amount. Mandatory crediting toward the final cost (VA-9006).

payment.productionGate.label: Production may be conditioned on payment (pay before copies / pay in full before release)
payment.productionGate.notes: Two express PROCESSING gates: (1) the >$200 deposit before continuing to process (VA-0031), and (2) prior unpaid balances 30+ days after billing before processing (VA-9004). No express statutory authorization for a general pay-in-full-before-release gate on the current request's final bill; the s…

payment.nonpayment.label: Nonpayment consequence (withdrawn after N days; prior-debt prepayment)
payment.nonpayment.notes: Virginia's nonpayment consequences: (a) deemed withdrawal after 30 days of non-response to a cost estimate (VA-9002 — tied to estimate non-response, not to a billed invoice); (b) prior-debt prepayment gate on future requests once a bill is 30+ days unpaid (VA-9004). No statutory withdrawal clock …

payment.reissue.label: Overrun re-issue rules (revised estimate required / blocks collection / restarts window)
payment.reissue.notes: Coverage: § 2.2-3704(A)-(J) full text read; § 2.2-3704.1 opened. No overrun/re-issue rule (no revised-estimate duty, no collection block, no window restart on variance). Actual-cost ceiling independently caps the final bill.

rules.maxFee.label: Request-level ceiling (actual cost cap / statutory max)
rules.maxFee.notes: The request-level ceiling is the body's actual cost incurred, reinforced by the lowest-possible-cost duty and the surplus-fee prohibition. No statutory dollar maximum.

rules.deMinimis.label: De-minimis: no charge below ($)
rules.deMinimis.notes: Coverage: § 2.2-3704(A)-(J) full text read; § 2.2-3704.1 opened. No de-minimis no-charge floor. rules.minFee.label: Minimum fee
rules.minFee.notes: Coverage: § 2.2-3704(A)-(J) full text read; § 2.2-3704.1 opened. No minimum-fee provision. A flat minimum fee exceeding actual cost on a small request would collide with the actual-cost ceiling (VA-0021) and the surplus-fee prohibition (VA-0023).

media.label: Electronic media (CD/DVD/USB) charge
media.notes: Electronic-media charges (CD/DVD/USB) are bounded by actual cost (F duplication/supplying; G for database-held records). delivery.label: Delivery: mail / handling / email / pickup
delivery.notes: Delivery costs fall under the actual cost of 'supplying' the records; no separate handling-fee authorization (a handling markup would be a surplus fee under VA-0023). Subsection G obliges e-mail/website delivery for electronic records where the body has the capability.

certification.label: Certification / certified-copy charge

av.label: Audio/video: per recording, per minute, free minutes

commercial.label: Commercial-purpose schedule (surcharge %, labor becomes chargeable)

waiver.forfeiture.notes: Coverage: § 2.2-3704(A)-(J) full text read; § 2.2-3704.1 opened. No fee-forfeiture-on-late-response provision. A failure to respond is a deemed DENIAL and a violation (§ 2.2-3704(E)) with enforcement consequences, but the statute never strips the body's ability to charge.

repeat.label: Repeat / aggregated requests (carry-forward, aggregation threshold)
repeat.notes: Coverage: § 2.2-3704(A)-(J) full text read; § 2.2-3704.1 opened. No repeat-request carry-forward or fee-aggregation threshold. The only cross-request linkage is the prior-debt prepayment gate (§ 2.2-3704(I), VA-9004), which is a payment gate, not aggregation.

fee.actual_cost_basis.summary: A public body may make reasonable charges not to exceed its actual cost incurred in accessing, duplicating, supplying, or searching for the requested records.

fee.actual_cost_basis.summary: The body shall make all reasonable efforts to supply the requested records at the lowest possible cost.
Any duplicating fee charged by a public body shall not exceed the actual cost of duplication.

fee.electronic_media_charge.summary: A body may make a reasonable charge, not exceeding actual cost, for records produced from a geographic information system at the request of anyone other than the owner of the subject land, except that it may charge on a pro rata per-acre basis for topographical maps it developed that encompass a …
fee.electronic_media_charge.clock_spec: ceiling: actual cost; exception — pro rata per-acre for body-developed topo maps over 50 contiguous acres

fee.no_charge_categories.summary: No public body shall impose extraneous, intermediary, or surplus fees or expenses to recoup the general costs of creating or maintaining records or transacting the general business of the public body.

custody.records_officer_designation.summary: All state, local, and regional public bodies subject to the chapter shall designate and publicly identify one or more FOIA officers to serve as the point of contact for records requests and to coordinate the body's FOIA compliance.
